item.title: OpenScreen: Free, Open-Source Screen Recording App with AI Editing
item.description:
OpenScreen: Free, Open-Source Screen Recording App with AI Editing

OpenScreen is a new open-source desktop application that turns raw screen recordings into polished demos without watermarks or subscriptions. It supports Windows, macOS, and Linux, offering features like AI-powered editing, automatic captions, and GPU-accelerated export.

📸 What It Does

OpenScreen is designed to help users record their screen and instantly transform the result into share-ready content for platforms like YouTube, X, Reddit, or documentation sites.

Key capabilities include:

  • Record a specific window or your entire screen
  • Capture both microphone and system audio
  • Webcam overlay with picture-in-picture mode
  • Auto and manual zooms with adjustable settings
  • Custom cursor size, smoothing, and click effects
  • Automatic on-device captions with offline transcription
  • An AI editing assistant that applies changes from natural language descriptions
  • Support for multiple background options including wallpapers and gradients
  • Motion blur and per-segment speed control on the timeline
  • Text, arrow, and image annotations with animation presets
  • Timeline snapping guides and audio waveform visualization
  • Export to MP4 or GIF with GPU-accelerated rendering (Metal, D3D11, Vulkan)

⚙️ Key Details

Feature Description
Licensing MIT License, 100% free for personal and commercial use
Platforms Windows, macOS, Linux
AI Assistant Works with Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Mistral, OpenRouter, MiniMax, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
CLI Support Headless recording, JSON editing, and rendering via command line
Caption Languages Arabic, Czech, English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Turkish, Vietnamese, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese

Development started with Siddharth Vaddem, who archived the original repository after v1.5.0 before moving development to a new repository under the same name and MIT license. The project remains actively maintained, though users should expect rough edges and occasional breaking changes to the project format and CLI.

item.title: NYT Cooking Launches AI Assistant for Recipe Customization and Ingredient Substitutions
item.description:
NYT Cooking Launches AI Assistant for Recipe Customization and Ingredient Substitutions

The New York Times has introduced an AI-powered assistant for its NYT Cooking app to help subscribers modify recipes and find ingredient substitutions. The tool is designed to provide practical cooking guidance based on reputable sources and user feedback rather than generating purely AI-generated recipes from scratch.

🔍 Overview

The assistant was trained on the New York Times archives, restaurant data, cookbooks, food columnists, and reader comments. Unlike purely AI-generated recipes, which the author found to be of poor quality, this tool is designed to work with existing, human-tested recipes. It is programmed not to comply with requests that the editors believe will result in a dish that tastes bad.

🧩 How it works

The feature appears as a small text box on the recipe page with the prompt “Customize this recipe…” Once a user enters a request, the assistant generates a modified version of the recipe:

  • New Title: It creates a unique title for the modified version (e.g., “One-Pot Chicken and Rice With Ginger and Green Beans”).
  • Non-destructive Editing: It leaves the original recipe unchanged and creates a separate entry.
  • Highlighting: All changes are highlighted under a “Your Version” tab.
  • Persistence: Users can flip back to the original recipe at any point.

⚙️ Key details

The assistant can handle a variety of tasks ranging from simple measurement conversions to complex dietary modifications.

Feature Description
Ingredient Swaps Suggests alternatives like Thai basil for cilantro or lime zest for makrut lime leaf.
Recipe Scaling Adjusts quantities to feed specific numbers of people, such as seven diners.
Dietary Changes Modifies existing recipes to be vegan or gluten-free.
Equipment Advice Provides suggestions for missing tools, such as a missing Bundt pan.
Measurement Conversion Converts metric weights to US measurements seamlessly.

While the tool is useful, it is not perfect; in one test, it incorrectly suggested halving the required butter for a cake. It also highlights how substitutions might change the flavor profile of a dish, such as noting that lime zest lacks the deep floral aroma of makrut lime leaf.

🚀 Availability

The tool is currently available to NYT Cooking subscribers. At launch, the assistant is accessible exclusively on the iOS version of the app.

#NYTCooking #ArtificialIntelligence #iOSApps #CookingTips

Source: NYT Cooking’s AI assistant saved my weeknight chicken, but almost ruined my cake
